name: Joinville

queries.query: Joinville Brazil official cadastral parcel map geoprocessamento cadastro imobiliario prefeitura SIMGeo
queries.scope: Identify first-party local land-registry/cadastral sources and safe anonymous parcel geometry.
queries.result: The official municipal SIMGeo page describes the city’s georeferenced information system and public map layers. The official SIMGeo ArcGIS REST sublayer simgeo/lotes/MapServer/3 is polygon geometry, supports Query/Data, and exposes safe objectid (OID) and iq parcel-key fields. A bounded anonymous point-intersection query at the unchanged WUP point returned one polygon (objectid 94825, iq 13-20-25-19-469); an independent returnIdsOnly query returned the same single OID. The layer response flagged exceededTransferLimit even though the ID-only point result contained one OID; the point query was spatially bounded and only the safe-ID geometry response was retained. No wider coverage or runtime qualification is claimed. Exact-ID follow-up query with where=objectid=94825 returned HTTP 200 and one polygon with the same id, iq, and identical geometry as the WUP-point response; this resolves the response-completeness ambiguity for the retained feature.
queries.executionMethod: Separate English-language web search followed by official-source review.

source.name: Joinville SIMGeo municipal cadastral lot polygons
source.serviceType: Official local cadastral/registry service reviewed; one bounded safe public parcel feature response verified Exact-ID read reproduced the point-query geometry.
source.nativeIdField: objectid (Esri OID); safe cadastral key iq
source.nativeIdEvidence: Official layer metadata exposes objectid as OID and iq as a string; bounded point-intersection query returned objectid 94825 / iq 13-20-25-19-469, confirmed by returnIdsOnly. A separate exact-ID read returned one feature and identical geometry.
source.scope: 201 distinct full native municipal lot polygons around the unchanged Joinville WUP locator across thirteen bounded cells; all grid and footprint geometries independently audited in EPSG32722. No invalidity, duplicate geometry or operation errors. One 0.01436m² shared-edge overlap was independently reproduced in native EPSG31982, with a maximum rectangle width below0.6mm; preserved without repair as a bounded reference-data caveat. Forced three-row paging, all201 fresh exact native-key reads, explicit absence, footprint lookup and source binding passed. This evidence does not establish citywide completeness, positional accuracy, legal title or currentness.
